clues: This is a neighbourhood in the west part of Kamloops, in British Columbia, Canada. It sits just north of the Thompson River.
This is the warmest small climate spot in its city. It can be four degrees warmer than another part of the same city.
For a short time, it was a district town of its own. Then it joined Kamloops in 1973.
It takes its name from a man from Liverpool, England. He lived here from 1896 to 1907.
Look north from its streets to see the Batchelor Hills. They mark the top edge of this part of the city.
